summary: Enterprise Suite AC-15 cloud readiness gate composes the local route manifest, in-memory harness, and ERP parity map into a deterministic pre-cloud report: local rehearsal readiness is true while cloud deployment readiness remains false with explicit blockers for listener/auth, durable storage, Postgres/RLS, Workflow/broker, statutory rails, runtime audit emission, deployment evidence, and SLO evidence.

findings: The gate is a small control-plane aggregator over existing typed seams and does not introduce runtime orchestration.
Cloud readiness is derived from explicit blockers rather than implicit booleans or prose.
The gate separates local rehearsal readiness from cloud deployment readiness, which is required for safe staged cloud integration.
Blockers enumerate platform-grade requirements: listener, auth, durable storage, RLS, Workflow/broker, statutory rails, runtime audit emission, deployment evidence, and SLO evidence.

F3_adversarial.diagnostic_asserted: Tests fail if local rehearsal inputs are missing, route/SAP counts drift, blocker inventory changes silently, or a cloud-ready flag bypasses unresolved blockers.
findings: Positive readiness report coverage and negative false-positive cloud-claim validation are both covered.
Developers can call enterprise_suite_cloud_readiness_report(), required_cloud_blockers(), and validate_cloud_claim() to understand exactly what remains before cloud deployment.
Focused readiness-gate tests/clippy, Enterprise Suite package-group tests/clippy, 25-package enterprise regression tests/clippy, fmt, data_class scan, and quality-marker scan passed.

alternatives_named: claim cloud readiness from route composition alone
wait for real cloud deployment before adding a gate
F6_alternatives.selected_rationale: The explicit gate lets later cloud work consume a typed blocker list without overclaiming deployment now.
rejected_reasons: Route composition alone omits auth, durable storage, Workflow/broker, statutory rails, audit emission, and SLO requirements.
Waiting for deployment would defer useful validation and make cloud integration absorb too many unknowns at once.

findings: No secrets, tenant data, network listener, auth bypass, provider SDK, or external storage are introduced.
Missing auth runtime and Postgres/RLS remain explicit blockers rather than hidden assumptions.

F8_performance.regression_baseline: Readiness report validates existing static route map, harness capabilities, and 23-row parity map; no I/O or hot runtime path exists.

findings.summary: Readiness computation is bounded by the 19-route catalog, 23 ERP rows, and fixed blocker vector.

findings: Public report fields carry data_class annotations and catalog row declares product-control plane metadata.
Statutory filing/disbursement rails and SLO evidence remain blockers, preventing premature compliance or cloud claims.
The change is additive: one readiness crate, catalog row, workspace membership, spec/tasks/evidence updates, and no external resources or migrations.
The report carries evidence refs for route composition, in-memory harness, and ERP parity map plus a named blocker vector for future dashboards.
Runtime audit-chain emission remains a blocker and non-claim; branch closeout uses static audit rows only.
Enterprise Suite AC-15 and D-12 record the staged migration boundary from local rehearsal to future cloud deployment.
The gate makes remaining cloud work explicit without changing service behavior or deployment state.

M1_challenge_assumption.premise_stated: A pre-cloud gate can safely mark local rehearsal ready while refusing cloud deployment claims if blockers are typed and tested.
M1_challenge_assumption.premise_evidence_ref: CS-ENT-SUITE-013 readiness tests and prior CS-ENT-SUITE-010/011/012 evidence refs
M1_challenge_assumption.do_nothing_consequence: Later cloud integration would rely on scattered non-claim prose instead of a deterministic blocker report.
M1_challenge_assumption.upstream_fix_rejection_reason: The route/harness/parity crates already own their local seams; the missing artifact is an aggregate readiness gate.

findings: This directly advances later Oyatie cloud integration by converting completed local foundations into an executable readiness boundary.
Names use cloud-readiness gate vocabulary and do not imply deployment.
Enterprise Suite spec, plan, todo, evidence, catalog, and audit-chain references were updated.
The crate is a control-plane governance artifact under Enterprise Suite and depends only on local composition/readiness inputs.
No listener, auth runtime, durable store, Postgres/RLS, provider SDK, Workflow engine/broker, child-service network client, cloud adapter, statutory rail, or runtime audit emitter was introduced.
No third-party dependencies were added; the crate depends only on existing Enterprise Suite local composition, harness, and ERP parity map crates.
No wire API schema is changed; the readiness gate exposes typed Rust control-plane records only.
Readiness computation deterministically validates route uniqueness, harness capabilities, ERP parity rows, and a fixed blocker inventory.
